properties.decision:
DECIDED by Anthony 2026-07-31, refining `dec:where-content-lives` (accepted) per `dec:reopen-supersedes`. The proposal and its measurement are preserved in the snapshot taken before this edit.

THE STORE IS HAND-ROLLED, SYNCHRONOUS, AND LIVES IN `reflow2-core`. Three operations — `put(bytes) -> hash`, `get(hash) -> bytes`, `exists(hash)` — over `sha2` (already a core dependency) and `std::fs`, with write-to-temp-then-rename for atomicity. Zero new crates.

WHY, MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED. `object_store` 0.14.1 with `default-features = false, features = ["fs"]` resolves 68 crates, **36 of them new to reflow2**. About 24 arrive through `url`'s internationalised-domain-name machinery — the whole ICU4X stack, `zerovec`/`yoke`/`tinystr`, `idna`, `percent-encoding` — which a local content-addressed store never calls. The accepted decision's note that cloud features off "avoids reqwest and the crypto providers" was true and did not describe the tree.

AND IT UN-DOES A COMPLICATION RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. `dec:where-content-lives` split hash-in-core from store-in-mcp ONLY because `object_store` is async and `fs` pulls tokio. A synchronous `std::fs` store keeps `reflow2-core` free of a runtime — measured, its entire dependency list is dynograph-{core,storage,graph,resolution,vector}, serde, serde_json, sha2 — and keeps the store deterministic and in-memory-testable alongside everything else in the core. THAT PART OF `dec:where-content-lives` IS SUPERSEDED; its other two parts (blobs committed to the repo; content-addressed, immutable, fail-loud pointers) STAND UNCHANGED.

`object_store` IS THE DOCUMENTED UPGRADE PATH, recorded rather than discarded. It is the right crate for multi-cloud object storage and remains the answer if a cloud backend is ever wanted: it presents one trait over local filesystem, in-memory, S3, GCS, Azure and HTTP/WebDAV, so the backend becomes runtime configuration. The three-function interface above is deliberately the shape it slots behind — content addressing is what makes the swap safe, because a blob fetched from anywhere verifies against its own hash. Adopting it later changes how bytes are fetched and nothing about what the graph says. WHEN THAT DAY COMES, the costs already measured apply: 36 new crates, an async runtime reaching the core (or the hash/store split reinstated), and a declaration per `dec:design-dependencies-declared`.

WHAT WE GIVE UP TODAY, stated so nobody rediscovers it: multipart uploads, conditional writes, listing and prefix semantics, and cloud backends. Immutable content-addressed blobs need none of them — there are no paths to list, no partial writes to resume, and no update-in-place to make conditional.
properties.name: Hand-rolled synchronous content store in reflow2-core, zero new dependencies; object_store is the documented upgrade path
properties.rationale:
Anthony's call on a measurement the accepted decision had itself demanded before adoption. That clause — "STILL TO CHECK BEFORE ADOPTING: its transitive tree with cloud features off MEASURED rather than assumed" — is the only reason this surfaced before code rather than after, and it is worth noting as a habit: a decision that names what it has NOT verified does work a confident decision would not.

The deciding argument was not dependency count for its own sake. It was that `object_store`'s value is uniformity across backends, and the feature set it exists to provide — paths, prefixes, listing, multipart, conditional writes — is precisely the set an immutable content-addressed store does not have. Paying 36 crates and an async runtime for capabilities the use case forecloses is the wrong trade at this size, and the trade reverses the moment a cloud backend is real.

Recorded as an upgrade path rather than a rejection, because the alternative to a hand-rolled store is not "no library forever" — it is "no library until there is something a library does better". Writing that down is what stops the next session re-running the same evaluation from scratch.
